hook: Alex Graves earned a degree in theoretical physics from the University of Edinburgh before completing a PhD in artificial intelligence at the Technical University of Munich, supervised by Jürgen Schmidhuber at the Dalle Molle Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research. During his doctoral work he introduced Connectionist Temporal Classification in 2006, a method that let recurrent neural networks train directly on unsegmented sequences such as speech and handwriting. In 2009 his CTC-trained LSTM networks became the first recurrent neural networks to win international handwriting recognition competitions. After postdoctoral work with Schmidhuber and with Geoffrey Hinton at the University of Toronto, he joined Google DeepMind in London as a research scientist, where he introduced the Neural Turing Machine and its successor, the Differentiable Neural Computer. In 2023 he published work on Bayesian Flow Networks and moved to InstaDeep as a Staff Research Scientist.

quick_facts: Holds a BSc in theoretical physics from the University of Edinburgh
Completed a PhD in artificial intelligence at the Technical University of Munich under Jürgen Schmidhuber
Introduced Connectionist Temporal Classification in 2006, now standard in speech and handwriting recognition
Created the Neural Turing Machine and the Differentiable Neural Computer while at Google DeepMind
Became a Staff Research Scientist at InstaDeep in 2023

achievements.title: Connectionist Temporal Classification
achievements.impact: Gave recurrent neural networks a way to train directly on unsegmented sequence data, becoming a foundational technique in modern speech and handwriting recognition systems.

achievements.title: Neural Turing Machines and Differentiable Neural Computer
achievements.impact: Introduced neural networks coupled to external memory, opening a line of research into models that can store and retrieve information the way a computer does.

achievements.title: Handwriting recognition breakthroughs
achievements.impact: Built CTC-trained LSTM systems that in 2009 became the first recurrent neural networks to win international pattern recognition competitions.

achievements.title: Supervised Sequence Labelling with Recurrent Neural Networks
achievements.impact: Wrote a 2012 reference text that consolidated CTC and related sequence labeling methods for the wider research community.
